first_request.user:
I'm characterizing how strongly rare chemical elements are integrated into the molecular skeleton of carcinogenic compounds. For every carcinogenic molecule that contains at least one atom of an element that appears in no other molecule in the database, I want the number of bonds its atoms of that element take part in. Please judge an element's rarity over every molecule in the database, carcinogenic or not. Return the molecule_id and that bond count for each qualifying molecule, one row per molecule, sorted by molecule_id.

BIRD evidence:
'+' is the label of a carcinogenic molecule, '-' of a non-carcinogenic one; a bond is a link between two atoms of a molecule.

No follow-up user is available. Give the best supported answer for the question. Return your final answer as exactly one fenced SQL block containing a single read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH query. Exclude intermediate SQL.

answer:
```sql
WITH rare_elements AS (
    SELECT element
    FROM atom
    GROUP BY element
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id) = 1
),
qualifying_molecules AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT m.molecule_id
    FROM molecule AS m
    JOIN atom AS a ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
    JOIN rare_elements AS r ON r.element = a.element
    WHERE m.label = '+'
),
rare_atoms AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT a.atom_id, a.molecule_id
    FROM atom AS a
    JOIN rare_elements AS r ON r.element = a.element
),
bond_counts AS (
    SELECT ra.molecule_id, COUNT(*) AS bond_count
    FROM rare_atoms AS ra
    JOIN connected AS c
      ON c.atom_id = ra.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = ra.atom_id
    GROUP BY ra.molecule_id
)
SELECT q.molecule_id, COALESCE(bc.bond_count, 0) AS bond_count
FROM qualifying_molecules AS q
LEFT JOIN bond_counts AS bc ON bc.molecule_id = q.molecule_id
ORDER BY q.molecule_id;
```

sql:
WITH atom_counts AS (
  SELECT
    molecule_id,
    COUNT(*) AS number_of_atoms,
    SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(element) = 'c' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS carbon_atoms,
    SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(element) = 'cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS chlorine_atoms
  FROM atom
  GROUP BY molecule_id
),
bond_counts AS (
  SELECT
    b.molecule_id,
    COUNT(*) AS number_of_bonds,
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN LOWER(a1.element) = 'c' OR LOWER(a2.element) = 'c' THEN 1
        ELSE 0
      END
    ) AS carbon_touching_bonds,
    SUM(CASE WHEN b.bond_type IN ('=', '#') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS multiple_bonds
  FROM bond AS b
  LEFT JOIN connected AS c ON c.bond_id = b.bond_id
  LEFT JOIN atom AS a1 ON a1.atom_id = c.atom_id
  LEFT JOIN atom AS a2 ON a2.atom_id = c.atom_id2
  GROUP BY b.molecule_id
),
qualified AS (
  SELECT
    m.molecule_id,
    m.label AS carcinogenicity_label,
    ac.number_of_atoms,
    COALESCE(bc.number_of_bonds, 0) AS number_of_bonds,
    ac.carbon_atoms,
    ac.chlorine_atoms,
    COALESCE(bc.carbon_touching_bonds, 0) AS carbon_touching_bonds,
    COALESCE(bc.multiple_bonds, 0) AS multiple_bonds
  FROM molecule AS m
  JOIN atom_counts AS ac ON ac.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
  LEFT JOIN bond_counts AS bc ON bc.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
  WHERE ac.carbon_atoms > 0
)
SELECT
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    ORDER BY carbon_touching_bonds DESC, number_of_atoms DESC, molecule_id ASC
  ) AS rank,
  molecule_id,
  carcinogenicity_label,
  number_of_atoms,
  number_of_bonds,
  carbon_atoms,
  chlorine_atoms,
  carbon_touching_bonds,
  multiple_bonds
FROM qualified
ORDER BY rank;

WITH bond_profile AS (
  SELECT
    b.bond_type AS bond_kind_symbol,
    COUNT(DISTINCT b.bond_id) AS bond_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE
      WHEN a1.element <= a2.element THEN a1.element || '|' || a2.element
      ELSE a2.element || '|' || a1.element
    END) AS element_pair_count
  FROM bond b
  JOIN connected c ON c.bond_id = b.bond_id
  JOIN atom a1 ON a1.atom_id = c.atom_id
  JOIN atom a2 ON a2.atom_id = c.atom_id2
  WHERE b.molecule_id = 'TR377'
    AND b.bond_type IN ('-', '=')
  GROUP BY b.bond_type
)
SELECT
  p.bond_kind_symbol,
  p.bond_count,
  p.element_pair_count,
  m.label AS carcinogenicity_label
FROM bond_profile p
JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id = 'TR377'
ORDER BY p.bond_count DESC, p.bond_kind_symbol ASC;

Please give me one row per element symbol with the element symbol and the number of such atoms, sorted alphabetically by element symbol. This should cover all compounds in the database. Note that an atom with no bonds at all doesn't count as being connected by single bonds, so exclude those.

BIRD evidence:
A single bond is a bond between two atoms sharing exactly one electron pair, denoted by the bond-type symbol '-'. A multiple bond is a double or triple bond, i.e. a bond between two atoms sharing more than one electron pair.

WITH atom_bond_status AS (
    SELECT

        a.element,
        COUNT(c.bond_id) AS bond_count,
        SUM(CASE WHEN b.bond_type = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS single_bond_count,
        SUM(CASE WHEN b.bond_type <> '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS multiple_bond_count
    FROM atom AS a
    LEFT JOIN connected AS c
        ON c.atom_id = a.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = a.atom_id
    LEFT JOIN bond AS b
        ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id
    GROUP BY a.atom_id, a.element
)
SELECT
    element,
    COUNT(*) AS atom_count

  AND single_bond_count = bond_count
  AND multiple_bond_count = 0

first_request.user:
In the toxicology compound database, which elements take part in a triple bond, and how widely are they distributed across the tested compounds? For each such element, give me its element symbol and the number of molecules that contain that element. Order the results from the most widespread element to the least; where two elements have equal counts, list them alphabetically by element symbol.

BIRD evidence:
The '#' bond-type symbol denotes a triple bond.

No follow-up user is available. Give the best supported answer for the question. Return your final answer as exactly one fenced SQL block containing a single read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH query. Exclude intermediate SQL.

answer:
```sql
SELECT a.element AS element_symbol, COUNT(DISTINCT a.molecule_id) AS molecule_count
FROM atom AS a
JOIN connected AS c ON c.atom_id = a.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = a.atom_id
JOIN bond AS b ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id
WHERE b.bond_type = '#'
GROUP BY a.element
ORDER BY molecule_count DESC, element_symbol ASC;
```

For molecule TR397, I want to see which elements form the bonding skeleton. For each element present among its atoms, how many atoms of that element take part in at least one bond? Please report two things per row: the element symbol (e.g. c, h, o) and the number of that element's atoms in TR397 that take part in a bond. One row per element, ordered alphabetically by element symbol. Only atoms belonging to TR397 should count.

BIRD evidence:
Takes part in a bond: the atom is one of the two atoms a bond joins.

answer:
```sql
SELECT a.element AS element, COUNT(DISTINCT a.atom_id) AS bonded_atom_count
FROM atom AS a
WHERE a.molecule_id = 'TR397'
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM connected AS c
    JOIN bond AS b ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id
    WHERE b.molecule_id = 'TR397'
      AND (c.atom_id = a.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = a.atom_id)
  )
GROUP BY a.element
ORDER BY a.element;
```
